daemon_enable.description: Whether to enable and start the arpon daemon automatically.

user.description: System user account under which arpon runs (must have minimal privileges).

group.description: System group associated with the arpon user.

pidfile.description: Absolute path to the file used to store the daemon's process ID.

interfaces.description: Network interface(s) to monitor for ARP traffic. Multiple interfaces may be listed.

log_file.description: Path to a dedicated log file. If empty, logging goes to syslog instead.

remote_log_host.description: Hostname or IP of a remote syslog server (leave blank to disable remote logging).

remote_log_port.description: UDP/TCP port used for remote syslog (typically 514).

mode.description: ARP inspection mode: 'dhcp' (DHCP Snooping-based), 'static' (static table), or 'hybrid' (both).

arp_table_path.description: Path to file containing static IP-to-MAC mappings (used in static/hybrid mode).

dhcp_lease_file.description: Path to the DHCP server lease file to monitor for ARP entries (used in dhcp/hybrid mode).

detect_spoof.description: Whether to detect ARP spoofing attempts (e.g., duplicate IPs, MAC mismatches).

prevent_spoof.description: Whether to actively block or drop malicious ARP packets (may affect network stability).

rescan_interval.description: Seconds between periodic re-checks of the ARP cache.

threshold.description: Number of suspicious ARP events before triggering an action.

anomaly_cmd.description: Optional command or script to run when an ARP anomaly is detected (e.g., '/usr/local/bin/alert-arp.sh').

whitelist.description: List of MAC addresses to exempt from ARP inspection.

items.description: MAC address in standard colon-separated format (e.g., '00:11:22:33:44:55')

fixed_arp.description: Static IP-to-MAC mappings to be registered with arpon regardless of mode.

start_delay.description: Seconds to wait after system boot before starting arpon (allows networking to stabilize).

daemon_opts.description: Extra command-line arguments to pass directly to the arpon binary (e.g., '-D -t 30').
